analysis:
This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md, in the Native Flint section (base lines ~2058-2069, head ~2058-2073). It documents that Flint always uses native KV and native checkpoint precision, ignoring the provider-wide defaults but refusing an explicit non-native per-model or env selection. It also documents that Flint is served only on paged attention: an automatic `engine_v2_kv_backend` selection for a verified FlintModel is treated as explicit paged, and explicit contiguous, the paged kill switch or a model-capability veto refuses the load. The patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not see the tail of the change.

Security review: no code, wire protocol, keys, attestation, authorization or encryption paths are modified, so no threat-model control (TB-002, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, A-001) is weakened. The prefix-cache threat T-041 (SSD tier, TTL, HMAC names) is not touched; the doc does not change checkpoint storage or cache policy. One availability-relevant point is that the load now refuses rather than falling back to contiguous. That is fail-closed behavior, not a regression. The documented behavior is a claim about EngineV2Factory.prepareProductionBackend and EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.resolve in code outside this diff, so I could not verify it. If those code changes ship in the same PR, the next pass should check that the refusal paths do not strand providers (T-057-like availability) and that the native-checkpoint override for Flint does not alter the at-rest encrypted cache semantics in T-041. Unchanged callers were not examined.
